newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - June 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - June 27.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Chinese political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Beijing. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (8610) 6532-1921. Fax: (8610) 6532-4978.
PEOPLE'S DAILY
- The National Committee of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference holds a meeting in Beijing to greet Hong Kong's return to the motherland.
- The 12th of a series of features on Hong Kong focuses on the spreading of patriotic education from primary school to universities in Hong Kong.
- A frontpage report says socialism is the only way for China to be powerful and prosperous.
FINANCIAL NEWS
- China's current account surplus in 1996 was $7.242 billion and the capital account surplus $39.967 billion.
- The Guangxi branch of the Agricultural Bank of China has extended another 400 million yuan in loans to the Guangxi Sugar Co for sugar reserves.
- The Daya Bay nuclear plant sets up its own financial company.
- The Ministry of Labour sets up a telephone hotline for people to report on irregularities in social security funds.
CHINA SECURITIES
- Fujian province issues rules to curb irregularities in stock brokerages.
ECONOMIC DAILY
- The State Planning Commission approves the construction of the 3.07 billion yuan Gaobazhou hydroelectric power plant in Hubei province.
- The national average price of wheat was 1,608 yuan in May, down 4.6 percent from April.
- Chinese customs is seizing a rising number of stamps smuggled in from Hong Kong.
ECONOMIC INFORMATION DAILY
- The Chinese cotton market is seen improving as demand climbs amid depressed output.
- China is to use a licensing system to regulate the silk industry, and plans to restructure the sector.
- Tin plate supply is seen exceeding demand in the next few years and experts call for no new production projects.
CHINA BUSINESS DAILY
- Smuggling of diesel fuel is increasing in coastal areas in Zhejiang and Fujian provinces.
XINHUA DAILY TELEGRAPH
- President Jiang Zemin has written a six-character inscription, which reads "Celebrate the Return of Hong Kong," for a July 1 rally in Beijing marking Hong Kong's return.
